builder_plan.scenario: A workflow needs specialist review, but extra agents may add more cost than useful work.
builder_plan.change: Test the proposed division of work against a single-agent implementation.
builder_plan.baseline: One agent with the same tools and an equal total token and time budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted outputs, coordination failures, wall-clock time, and total cost across all agents.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: FedReady: Bounded Agents for Federation Formation
summary: The method replaces manual, per-study federation formation (site selection, contract and adapter authoring, task-code preparation) with bounded LLM agents whose artifacts the runtime accepts only after digest-tied checks. It costs an agent orchestration layer, repeated verification passes, and LLM inference for every new target, and adds no benefit once sites and artifacts are fixed because conventional federated training then proceeds without the agents. It can fail through false-positive site admission (19 development failures are analyzed, and discovery precision is only 0.65), incorrect runtime-generated contracts, and dependence on site-private mappings that cannot be validated cross-site.
rationale: The results come from 39 simulated sites in a single medical-imaging domain, so a small team without an existing federated-learning deployment should treat this as a niche orchestration pattern to monitor rather than adopt or test now.
technique: Bounded LLM agents for FL site preparation

claims.statement: The method replaces manual, per-study federation formation (site selection, contract and adapter authoring, task-code preparation) with bounded LLM agents whose artifacts the runtime accepts only after digest-tied checks. It costs an agent orchestration layer, repeated verification passes, and LLM inference for every new target, and adds no benefit once sites and artifacts are fixed because conventional federated training then proceeds without the agents. It can fail through false-positive site admission (19 development failures are analyzed, and discovery precision is only 0.65), incorrect runtime-generated contracts, and dependence on site-private mappings that cannot be validated cross-site.

Across 39 simulated retinal sites and four tasks, discovery reaches recall 1.00 at precision 0.65; eligibility verification removes all 17 false positives without losing an eligible site-task pair; maximum survival-curve difference versus the manual reference is 0.001133.
